clue.text: Time to settle back what's owed

indicators.note: back here tells us the word for settle is read from right to left

parts.note: to bed down is to settle for the night, so settle gives bed

explanation.surface: A demand that the time has come to pay off what you owe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for settle, and the time abbreviation then goes after it although the clue names Time first. 'settle' looks like paying up, fitting the debt surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is a sum of money owing to someone.

clue.text: Saudi, Abu Dhabi .. it's around there somewhere

definitions.text: Saudi, Abu Dhabi .. it's around there somewhere

indicators.note: somewhere says those letters are present but not in order, so they must be rearranged
the letters sit there in the run of the place names, the end of Saudi running into Abu and the start of Dhabi

parts.note: the five letters I, A, B, U, D run across these words

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely gestures at a map of the Gulf, naming Saudi Arabia and Abu Dhabi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around there' points to IABUD inside 'Saudi, Abu Dhabi'; 'somewhere' says to rearrange those letters. The whole clue is also the definition, since the emirate lies between Saudi Arabia and Abu Dhabi.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf emirate lies just along the coast from Abu Dhabi, near Saudi Arabia, so the whole description locates it.

clue.text: Fundamentalist ran a bingo game

indicators.note: game is read as a verb or adjective meaning willing to play about, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious fundamentalist runs a bingo night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is the anagram signal for RAN A BINGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelical fundamentalists often describe themselves as having been spiritually reborn.

clue.text: Animals disturbed pumas lairs

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of the following words are mixed

explanation.surface: Animals are upset when someone disturbs the dens of pumas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' signals an anagram of PUMAS LAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsupials, such as kangaroos, are a class of pouched mammals, so animals defines them by category.

clue.text: An environmentalist needing new suit

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving A

indicators.note: needing means lacking, so the letter for new is taken away

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmentalist party

explanation.surface: An eco-campaigner needs a fresh outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' here means 'wanting' in the sense of lacking: A GREEN loses its N to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit and to agree are synonyms when food or a climate is said to agree with someone.

clue.text: One looking for a scrap, to wit seeker of retribution

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely or to wit
an avenger is one who seeks revenge

explanation.surface: A man spoiling for a fight, who turns out to be pursuing revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight, but here it is a discarded bit of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger hunts through rubbish for leftovers worth keeping.

clue.text: Sparkling waters in draught a source of energy

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for draught

parts.note: a draught is a drink, as is a potion

indicators.note: sparkling suggests the letters fizz about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Fizzy water in a drink gives you a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparkling' scrambles the water word into WERSTA, and 'in' splits the drink word after its second letter. 'Sparkling waters' reads like mineral water, which is the surface's trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A power station is a plant that generates electricity for a grid.

clue.text: Bitter sound of a Slav

indicators.note: sound of says the word is identified by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: a Serb is one of the Slavic peoples of the Balkans

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that an Eastern European man sounds bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound of' signals a homophone: 'a Serb' said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare variant of acerbic, meaning sour or harsh in taste or tone.

clue.text: Wetland plants around Eastern Latvia's borders

indicators.note: around means the plant word surrounds the two abbreviations

parts.note: sedges are grassy plants of marshes and wet ground
LV is the international vehicle code for Latvia

explanation.surface: Marsh plants grow along the frontiers of eastern Latvia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the plant word round the two abbreviations. 'borders' seems to belong to Latvia's frontiers but is the definition, the edges of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Selvedges are the woven edges of a fabric that stop it fraying, so they are its borders.

clue.text: Return of dull poet

indicators.note: return of says the word for dull is turned to run backwards

parts.note: drab means dull or colourless

explanation.surface: A tedious poet makes a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' reverses DRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, as Shakespeare is called the Bard.

clue.text: Bill in short trousers to trail behind means to get fit

indicators.note: in puts the word for bill inside the shortened trousers
short means the word for trousers loses its last letter

parts.note: trews are close-fitting tartan trousers worn in Scotland
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up
to heel is to follow close behind, as a dog does

explanation.surface: A man called Bill, in shorts, jogs behind others to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' makes TREW; 'in' puts the bill inside that, giving TREADW. 'Bill' looks like a man's name, and trews are tartan trousers worn in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadwheel is a wheel turned by stepping on it, like a treadmill used for exercise.

clue.text: Favourites coming back to work a sudden change

indicators.note: coming back says the word for favourites is read in reverse

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets
to function is to work or operate

explanation.surface: Favoured staff return to the office after a sudden shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses the favourites word. 'Favourites coming back to work' reads like staff returning, but the definition is a mathematical term.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a step function jumps abruptly from one value to another, an abrupt shift rather than a smooth slope.

clue.text: Russian butcher cooked then ate liver swallowing cut of meat

indicators.note: swallowing means the anagram takes another piece inside it
cooked suggests the words are prepared and rearranged like ingredients

parts.note: a rib is a cut of meat, as in rib of beef

explanation.surface: A Russian meat seller prepared a meal and ate liver along with a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges THEN ATE LIVER; 'swallowing' sets RIB inside the result. 'butcher' is not a tradesman but a murderous tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsar Ivan IV of Russia was notorious for his cruelty and mass killings.

clue.text: Note one cheating at cards

definitions.meaning: a musical note raised a semitone
a card ... is a professional cheat at card games

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a raised musical note and a swindler at card tables, as in card sharp.

clue.text: Barge around having great estates, something above criticism

indicators.note: around means the word for barge encloses the other piece

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed barge
acred means owning land, as in a well-acred family

explanation.surface: A barge travels round the land of a wealthy landowner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the barge round the estates word after its first letter. ACRED is an old word for owning much land, little used today.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea or institution treated as beyond question.

clue.text: It will avert the worst consequences of a strike

definitions.text: It will avert the worst consequences of a strike

parts.words: It will avert the worst consequences of a strike
parts.note: a strike seems to be industrial action, but it is a bolt from a thunderstorm, and the device protects buildings from it

explanation.surface: Something that will head off the damage caused by a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests a labour dispute; the device is a metal rod that carries a storm's discharge safely to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: This rod on a roof carries a bolt from a storm safely down to earth, preventing fire and damage.

clue.text: Large American phone company given sweetener forming network

parts.note: AT&T is the big American telecoms company, giving ATT
icing is a sugary coating for cakes

explanation.surface: A big US telecoms firm is offered an inducement to build a network.
explanation.walkthrough: AT&T's ampersand is dropped, leaving ATT. 'sweetener' suggests a bribe but is a sugar topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Latticing is crisscross work of strips, making a grid or mesh pattern.

clue.text: Batting side's first man playing wide ball approaching stumps

parts.note: in cricket the side that is in is batting

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word side's

parts.note: a winger plays on the wide flank of a football or rugby team

explanation.surface: A cricket team's opening batsman is a winger in another sport.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an inswinger is a ball that curves in toward the batsman's stumps, the three wooden posts behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery that swerves in the air toward the batsman, heading for the wicket, is what bowlers call this.

clue.text: See 14
In news agency a thousand things to be done

indicators.note: In says the thousand sits inside the news agency name

parts.note: TASS is the Russian state news agency
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: A news agency has a thousand jobs on its list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' places K inside TASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work or duties that must be carried out.

clue.text: On onset of illness single doctor gets out medical specialist

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order and rearranged
onset of picks the first letter of the word illness

explanation.surface: At the start of an illness, a lone doctor goes off to find a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ON, I (onset of illness), SINGLE and DOCTOR and rearrange them all; 'out' is the anagram signal and 'gets' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An endocrinologist is a doctor who treats glands and hormone disorders.

clue.text: Gull swallowing last of leftover fruit

indicators.note: swallowing means the word for gull takes a letter inside it

parts.note: to gull is to dupe or trick someone

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word leftover

explanation.surface: A seagull gulps down the remains of some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gull' looks like the seabird but is a verb, to trick. 'swallowing' puts R inside DUPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A drupe is a fleshy fruit with a stone, such as a plum or cherry.

clue.text: Old time to give up humming

parts.note: Lent is the season before Easter when Christians give up luxuries

explanation.surface: An elderly person decides it is time to quit humming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humming' here means smelling, the slang sense of a strong odour, not singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Olent is an old word for smelling or giving off a scent, and humming is slang for stinking.

clue.text: One sucking up a drop of drink in amusement

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside the word for amusement

parts.note: a toy is a plaything, something for amusement

indicators.note: a drop of drink is only its first little bit, the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone sips a drink for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and D inside TOY. 'sucking up' looks like drinking but means flattering.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a fawning flatterer who curries favour with those in power.

clue.text: In circus acrobatically set end of trapeze for gymnastic exercises

indicators.note: In says the following pieces go inside the jumbled word
acrobatically suggests the letters tumble and land in a new order

parts.note: to fix is to set something firm

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word trapeze

explanation.surface: At the circus, a trapeze act is staged as part of a gymnastics routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acrobatically' scrambles CIRCUS to CRUCIS; 'In' sets the setting word plus E (end of trapeze) inside it, before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: In gymnastics, crucifixes are moves on the rings where the arms are held straight out sideways.

clue.text: Odd characters from Algeria in Indian city

indicators.note: odd characters are the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word Algeria

explanation.surface: Some strange people from Algeria turn up in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' look like strange people but are the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is the city in northern India where the Taj Mahal stands.

clue.text: Little Scots horsemen appearing most evenings

parts.note: wee is the Scots word for little
knights were mounted soldiers, so horsemen

explanation.surface: Small Scottish riders show up on most nights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most evenings' means the evenings of most of the week, Monday to Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeknights are the evenings from Monday to Friday, which make up most of the week.

clue.text: Vehicle that could back up enclosed space

indicators.note: back up in a down light would read upward, but here in an across it simply means reverse the word

parts.note: a yard is an enclosed area beside a building

explanation.surface: A truck reversing into a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back up' reverses YARD; it looks like a vehicle reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low, heavy cart, traditionally used by brewers to deliver barrels.
